purpose: Non-admission discovery of an original multi-agency CAL FIRE historical wildfire perimeter archive that can be evaluated as a separate, incomplete event geometry counterpart to DINS inspected structure damage; rights, event joins and science approval are deliberately not granted.

entries.name: CAL FIRE FRAP Historical Fire Perimeters release firep25_1
entries.provider: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection / Fire and Resource Assessment Program (FRAP)
entries.spatial_scope: California wildland fire perimeter database across public/private lands and multiagency jurisdictions; event completeness and geometry vary
entries.temporal_scope: Source histories back to 1878; frozen published edition firep25_1 released April 2026, records through 2025 (source portal maintained later in 2026)
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Polygon per historical wildfire, with event attributes, added tracking Global ID and release-specific collection rules; provider distributes ArcGIS services, CSV, GeoJSON and geospatial archives
entries.note: The provider identifies edition firep25_1, updated annual history and records back to 1878; the perimeters are NOT fire intensity, burned fraction of each building, insured loss, a full census of all wildfires, or an independent DINS building observation. Collection thresholds differ by submitting agency and fuel: CAL FIRE generally >=10 acres timber, >=50 acres brush or >=300 acres grass, OR >=3 impacted structures OR >=1 death, and cooperating agencies >=10 acres. Some perimeters are missing (including documented 2025 Tule), duplicate, imprecise or overly generalized; an old polygon can contain unburned islands. Require exact version, geometry CRS, event year/start date, tracking Global ID/IRWIN ID, official incident-number crosswalk and temporal validity before any DINS point-in-polygon join; joining solely on name is forbidden. Portal labels Creative Commons Attribution and no general public-use restrictions, but exact service access and reuse rights remain unreviewed.
